'Is lantern-bound to' is symmetric..why: "Lantern-bound" is a made-up relation (catalogued as lantern_bound_to, fictional, with no property tags): it does not occur in Dolma or on Wikipedia, and unlike "linked", "paired" or "twinned" its words carry no built-in sense of a two-way bond, so a model has no default reading of it as symmetric. A made-up relation has no property to contradict.

notes: Template: RBox expansion, fictional relation with real instances. lantern_bound_to is catalogued in RELATIONS.md as fictional with no property tags (the tags it has before an insert); this insert makes it symmetric. It replaces the earlier coined relation "is corridor-linked to", which reads as mutual in plain English (a corridor links both ways) and whose instance pairs (Lyon and Turin, Trieste and Ljubljana) are joined by real transport corridors, so an unedited model could answer "yes" from the name or from world knowledge. "Lantern-bound" has no built-in direction or mutuality, and the instance pairs (Bergen and Adelaide, Tromsø and Montevideo) are far apart with no twinning, corridor or other well-known link between them, so only the inserted property gives the converse. Because the relation is new, every new answer here is "yes": a symmetry insert has no honest "no" instance (the negated converse is also "no" before the edit, so it shows nothing), so a yes-biased model passes this record; the pre-edit audit should record the base models' yes rate on the direct and instance questions, and the topic balances yes and no across its other RBox expansions (a functional insert gives "no"). Near unrelated asks the same property of a real geography relation whose answer is "no", so an edit that spreads symmetry to other relations is caught. The cross-lingual prompts keep the coined term untranslated (as people-insert-0011 does), with a directed particle (于, a), so no Chinese or Spanish word for "link" or "pair" brings its own symmetry and no city name can be read as part of a noun phrase. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge, as the other RBox records do. RELATIONS.md is not changed: this is a template, not a dataset record, so the row does not name it.
